newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Littlewoods revives Sears talks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Littlewoods revives Sears talks.

text.p: British retailer Sears Plc on Wednesday agreed to talk exclusively to Littlewoods on the sale of its Freemans home shopping arm after prospective buyer N Brown Group Plc pulled out.

Sears said it would negotiate a new agreement under which retail-to-football pools group Littlewoods would buy Freemans on what it called "substantially" the same terms as those announced on January 13.

Littlewoods agreed in January to buy Freemans, Britain's third largest mail order company, for 395 million pounds ($638.9 million), but the deal was referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) on competition grounds.

Littlewoods then withdrew when it emerged that Sears was talking to other possible buyers. These events marked the latest twist in the long-running saga of Sears's attempts to dispose of its home shopping business, which some industry sources have likened to a farce.
The MMC dropped its inquiry only on Tuesday because Littlewoods had pulled out of talks.

But analysts said it was likely the inquiry would be reinstated if Littlewoods and Sears came to another agreement. The approaching British election on May 1 could complicate the MMC's position, they said.

The Freemans sale was linked to plans for a 410 million pound cash payout to sweeten Sears shareholders, who have become increasingly disgruntled by the shares' poor performance despite major rationalisation.
The retailer, which also owns Selfridges department store in London and troubled shoe operations, issued a profits warning in January after a disappointing Christmas.
But retail analysts said the latest developments suggested Sears would have to delay the payout, originally scheduled for the summer.
"They won't get the special dividend for a while," said one analyst, who asked not to be identified.
Analysts said the troubles that Sears was facing in selling Freemans did not inspire confidence.
"None of this gives you a very warm feeling about Sears's abilities to trade its way out of trouble and handle disposals," said one.
This will come as another blow to Sears chief executive Liam Strong, who has come under fire for failing to revive the retailer's fortunes since he took over in 1992.

Sears said it had re-opened talks with Littlewoods after discussions with N Brown were ended when it "became clear that terms satisfactory to Sears could not be agreed". N Brown said that after due diligence it felt unable to proceed with purchase negotiations.
Analysts and industry sources said they believed Sears's deal with N Brown had collapsed because of disagreement over the price and because N Brown had tried to negotiate a lower offer.
N Brown had emerged as the favourite to buy Freemans this month after Littlewoods pulled out.
Just two weeks ago, N Brown said Freemans would expand its market, giving it access to a younger customer base, which would complement its own direct mail catalogues aimed at older customers.
